claim: A municipal body assumes an affirmative duty of care toward pedestrians when it has received repeated written notice of a hazardous sidewalk condition and fails to remediate it within a reasonable time. The Ninth Circuit held that the Tucson City Council's eighteen-month inaction following documented complaints brought it within the scope of actionable negligence under Arizona tort principles.
citation: Aberfoyle v. Tucson City Council, 683 F.3d 441 (9th Cir. 2011)
initial_reasoning: The Aberfoyle v. Tucson City Council case directly addresses the issue of a municipal body's affirmative duty of care toward pedestrians when it receives repeated written notice of a hazardous sidewalk condition and fails to remediate it within a reasonable time. The Ninth Circuit's holding in this case establishes Arizona tort principles that support the claim, specifically that eighteen months of inaction following documented complaints constitutes actionable negligence. The case provides a clear legal basis for the claim.
